entities.summary: Narayanapala was the seventh emperor of the Pala Empire, ruling from 927 CE to his death. He expanded the empire's influence to the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent and established trade relations with neighboring kingdoms. The Pala Empire under Narayanapala reached its peak during his reign, with significant cultural, economic, and religious developments. The empire's capital, Mahasthangarh, became a major center of Buddhist learning and art. Narayanapala's reign also saw the translation of important Buddhist texts into the local languages, contributing to the spread of Buddhism in the region. His legacy as a just and wise ruler was cemented by the numerous inscriptions and monuments erected during his reign, which continue to fascinate historians and scholars today.
